newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUMBLE AGAINST TEENAGE PACEMAN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA CRUMBLE AGAINST TEENAGE PACEMAN.

text.p: Australia's preparation for next week's second test against England suffered a setback on Saturday as the tourists slumped to 220 for eight in awkward conditions against Leicestershire.
In overcast conditions, 19-year-old fast bowler Jimmy Ormond caused the Australians major problems, swinging the ball alarmingly at times on the first day of their three-day match.
Captain Mark Taylor, who sat out the tourists' last drawn match against Nottinghamshire after scoring a century in the first test, made just one before he was yorked with the score on 10.

Mark Waugh, who twice fell cheaply in Australia's nine-wicket loss to England in the first test, managed just six before becoming Ormond's fifth victim. The teenager, playing in just his fourth first class match, finished with six for 54.
"That's the biggest day by far I've had in cricket -- in fact I bowled some rubbish too, but there were some jaffers," he said.
"I have swung it as much before, but my best bowling in my three previous first class matches was only two for 60.
"The wicket I enjoyed most was Taylor's -- it was a yorker that went right through him."
Ormond was only called into the team two days ago in place of injured David Millns.
Ricky Ponting at least managed to master the conditions, hitting 64 from 116 balls.
